references.text: Moses reminds Israel to remember what Amalek did to them when they came out of Egypt, and commands them to blot out the memory of Amalek.
Balaam's prophecy about Amalek as the first among the nations, but destined to perish forever.
God commands Saul to punish Amalek for what they did to Israel when they came up from Egypt.
Amalek's origin as a son of Eliphaz and Timna, descendants of Esau.
Saul fought against Amalek and delivered Israel from those who plundered them.
The Amalekites attacked Ziklag and took David's families captive, showing the ongoing hostility between Amalek and Israel.
The context for Amalek's attack—Israel had just camped at Rephidim and quarreled with Moses over water.
This verse marks the end of the same journey episode where Amalek attacked, showing that Israel survived the battle at Rephidim before moving on to Sinai.
Highlights the long-standing and repeated hostility from Amalek toward Israel that began at Rephidim.
Confirms the same travel event and timing of departure from Rephidim as mentioned in Exodus 17.
Sets the context for the battle at Rephidim by describing the arrival and the subsequent lack of water that triggered God's intervention.
